skill.description: Use AXe CLI patterns to automate iOS Simulator gestures, text input, screenshots, video capture, and accessibility inspection.

skill.author: 0xBigBoss

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown command examples or inline backticks, not hidden code execution. Real residual risks are the third-party AXe installation and expected simulator capture or UI inspection commands, which can expose sensitive test data.

remediation.suggestion: Document the trusted AXe source, pin installation guidance to a reviewed release, and recommend checksum or release verification before use.

remediation.issue: Simulator screenshots, videos, and UI dumps can expose data
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to run capture and describe-ui commands only on test simulators with non-production accounts and sanitized data.

remediation.issue: Example form flow includes a sample password value
remediation.suggestion: Replace concrete password examples with placeholders and remind users not to put real secrets in prompts or command history.

content.user_title: Automate iOS Simulator Testing with AXe
content.value_statement: iOS simulator testing often needs repeatable taps, text entry, screenshots, and accessibility checks. This skill provides AXe CLI command patterns for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
actual_capabilities: Install AXe CLI with Homebrew using the documented tap.
List iOS simulators and route commands to a selected UDID.
Tap, swipe, gesture, and press hardware buttons in the simulator.
Type text from direct input, stdin, files, or HID key sequences.
Capture screenshots, record video, and stream simulator frames.
Inspect accessibility trees for the full screen or a point.
limitations: Requires macOS, Xcode Simulator, Homebrew, and the AXe binary.
Commands operate on simulator instances, not physical iOS devices.
It does not validate app behavior or accessibility results by itself.
Screenshots, videos, and UI descriptions may contain sensitive test data.

use_cases.title: Repeat Simulator Smoke Tests
use_cases.description: Run predictable taps, swipes, text entry, and screenshots during manual release checks.

use_cases.title: Capture App States Quickly
use_cases.description: Record simulator video or screenshots after key UI actions for bug reports and design review.

use_cases.title: Inspect Accessibility Structure
use_cases.description: Read the accessibility tree and check labels, identifiers, and element locations during audits.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Simulator
prompt_templates.prompt: Use axe-ios-simulator to list available simulators and help me choose a UDID for testing.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use AXe to tap Continue, type sample text, and take a screenshot in the selected simulator.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Accessibility
prompt_templates.prompt: Describe the current simulator UI with AXe, summarize missing labels, and suggest safer selectors for automation.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Repeatable Test Script
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an AXe command sequence that waits for a target element, scrolls until visible, fills a test form, records video, and captures a final screenshot.

output_examples.input: Capture the state after I submit the test form.
output_examples.output: The result includes the selected simulator, the action sequence, a final screenshot path, and notes about visible success or error states.

output_examples.input: Check whether the current screen exposes useful accessibility labels.
output_examples.output: The result summarizes the visible accessibility tree, highlights missing labels, and names stable identifiers for future automation.

output_examples.input: Record a short simulator video for a bug report.
output_examples.output: The result describes the recording settings, the saved video location, and any sensitive UI areas to review before sharing.

best_practices: Use dedicated test simulators and test accounts before capturing screenshots or video.
Prefer accessibility identifiers over coordinates when the app provides stable labels.
Review each generated command before execution, especially install, file, and media commands.
anti_patterns: Do not run capture commands on simulators that contain production data.
Do not hard-code real passwords, tokens, or customer data in text input examples.
Do not depend only on coordinates when labels or identifiers are available.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It guides AXe CLI usage for simulator taps, gestures, typing, screenshots, video, and accessibility inspection.

faq.question: Does it work on real iPhones?
faq.answer: No. The documented commands target iOS Simulator instances through a simulator UDID.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it install software automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents a Homebrew install command that users should review before running.

faq.question: Can it inspect accessibility labels?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows AXe commands for full-screen and point-based accessibility descriptions.

faq.question: What data should I protect?
faq.answer: Protect simulator screenshots, videos, UI dumps, typed text, and any files used for input.
